Cursed Strikes drops like an anvil on anyone trying to block or wake up from the floor, crashing straight through Vessel's enemies block to deal heavy damage while trading unsafety for pure block breaking. Vessel leaps up and drives a downward dropkick straight into the floor, slamming whoever gets in the way for 14 damage. While this move is unblockable, bypasses ragdoll, and disables lock-on, it is interruptible, cannot be feinted after downward motion or aimed straight down being heavily punishable on whiff and if Vessel's opponent has evasive, and runs on a 14-second cooldown. Serving as incredible finish tool. But often being used for fast movement for after feinting the move.

Crushing Blow charges cursed energy in Vessel's hand to slam the floor, grabbing nearby opponents by the torso and smashing them down twice before throwing them skyward. Vessel slams the opponent to the ground, grabbing nearby enemies to smash them down twice before tossing them upward for 12 total damage (6 per slam), or releasing a lower-damage shockwave for 3 damage if no target is grabbed. While this move is unblockable and bypasses ragdoll, it is interruptible during startup, having an incredibly small hitbox, often fails to drive the opponent upward if debris are around, and runs on a 15-second cooldown. Often being used as a green M1 reset

Crushing Blow dashes across the mid-air creating spacing slamming down to grab targets and perform ground slams, functioning as a airborne combo tool. Vessel dashes through the air to slam down on enemies, executing the same ground slam sequence as normal Crushing Blow for 12 total damage (6 per slam) or releasing a 3 damage shockwave on miss. While this move bypasses ragdoll, it is blockable from all sides and interruptible, but allows Vessel to feint during the initial hop to gain good amount of forward air movement and drive forward for great mobility, sitting on a 15-second cooldown.

Divergent Fist winds back Vessel's arm to throw a heavy physical strike that is quickly followed by a second, delayed wave of cursed energy to knock the enemy away. Vessel winds back their arm to deliver a blow before a second burst of cursed energy triggers, dealing 10 total damage (5 per hit). While the initial hit is blockable, the move is semi-blockable, interruptible, and partly bypasses ragdoll because the second unblockable burst bypasses shields—making it uniquely effective for punishing opponents who block all the time. Additionally, if the delayed cursed energy interrupts an opponent's action, it triggers the Interruption Variant, which bypasses ragdoll, becomes unblockable, deals 5 damage, and stuns the target briefly instead of sending them flying, all on an 18-second cooldown.

Black Flash pulls Vessel's fist back while their body flashes white, releasing a strong strike that blasts the target away upon timing a second input. Vessel pulls back their fist and flashes white, releasing, high-impact punch on a second key press to deal 10 base damage and send enemies flying. While this move is unblockable, interruptible, and cannot bypass ragdoll, it functions mainly as a solid combo tool that rewards sharp timing—doubling its impact to 20 damage if it successfully interrupts an enemy's active move (excluding blocking)—all running on a same 18-second cooldown. But being Really easy to punish on evasive.

Black Flash Chain strikes Vessel's opponent's back with cursed sparks to stun them in place, keeping the move available to unleash up to four consecutive Black Flashes in a row. Vessel connects with an opponent's back, stunning them instead of knocking them down and allowing up to four continuous strikes, ending in a heavy finisher. The initial strikes deal 7 damage (14 on interruption) while the fourth blow deals 15 damage, resetting Vessel's side dash cooldown after each successful chain hit. While this variant is unblockable, interruptible, features true ragdoll, and cannot bypass ragdoll, it is used far more often than normal Black Flash to pull off stylish combos, though it is extremely easy to punish and becomes very unreliable against decent players who know how to react, all operating on an 18-second cooldown.

Manji Kick raises Vessel's arm and leg to adopt a defensive stance, parrying incoming strikes into a sharp upward Taido roundhouse kick or swooping aerial counter. Vessel enters a guarded posture to evade incoming attacks, striking back with an upward roundhouse kick on melee hit to knock the target sideways, or spinning through the air to close distance and strike if an bullet projectiles hits Manji Kick Vessel's leaps in the air to kick the opponent. Dealing 8.5 damage, this attack is unblockable, bypasses ragdoll, features true ragdoll, can hit secondary enemies caught in the path, and operates on a 0.6s counter window. While it stands as a decent counter option in Vessel's kit, it cannot be feinted, leaving Vessel vulnerable if baited, sitting on a 20-second cooldown.

Hello! Welcome to the Writing Guide of Dogslamloop Wiki. Here, you will learn about the basics of writing things for the wiki. Or maybe you are here to remind yourself of the Guide. Either way, this Writing Guide aims to create a baseline for every articles in the wiki, a standard of Dogslamloop.

While this Guide sets up a baseline for every article to follow, individual character pages might have some difference in the tones they use. You can say it is a "vibe" of those character pages. Anyway, so long as these tones don't undermine or break the baseline set by the Guide, they are fine to stay; and if you want to contribute, you can also consider following the tone set by those who come earlier (Inconsistent tones would be ground for rejection, unless you touched up the entire page)

Try to avoid personal and casual language Speak as though you're objectively correct and are the authority. Don't use words like "basically" or "idk" and the like Avoid speaking in first person (using the 'I' or 'me' pronoun) [b]As much as possible[/b], avoid addressing the player directly. Say "Honored One can combo" instead of "You can combo" You can joke around a little bit but don't get to the point where information is bogged down by humor Refer to the character as their [b]in-game JJS name[/b] ([s]Yuji[/s], Vessel) Please capitalize proper nouns ([s]granite blast[/s], Granite blast) Writing should be treated like writing professionally, but not over the top. Something on the level of High School/College essay would be high enough for the site [b]Do not use hateful language, slurs, discriminatory terms, and similar things. Use your common sense[/b]

It would also be good that when talking about a skill or something in a Base kit of a character, you should try your best to not mention ult (with the exception of ult bar). Especially when the site allows for switching between base and ult movesets

Beside the character pages, every other pages that are open to edit publicly on the site should follow a strict uniform technical tone instead. You can mention or refer to the reader in those pages as well as they concern something else that is not a character (Fundamentals, HUD, Frame Data, Private Server Setting, etc.)

Usage of undefined Buzzwords that are not in the Terminologies Page (Punch Kick Merchant, Ragdoll Kicker, etc.) Wrong usage of terms in Terminologies (Head of the Hei is a Zoner, Linking Blood Edge after an Uppercut is a popular Tech, etc.) Disregard for following the basics of the Guide (I personally would use this xyz combo, etc.) Usage of non-technical/troll medias (Using Medias that don't follow the Guide) Troll Submission (Repeated offenses might get you barred from submitting) Inconsistent tones Putting outdated information (Cursed Strikes can M1 reset, etc.) Making technical claims with zero to little backing/evidence (You can evasive punish Lapse Blue on Hit, etc.) Bad Grammar & Spelling ([color=hsl(0, 100%, 80%)]Veesel[/color] cna destroyly kill [color=hsl(272, 43%, 64%)]Luck Coward[/color], etc.)

"[b]Cancel[/b]" cancels whatever you are doing and bring you back to the latest page you are in or the page you are editting, Auto-save will fire and save what you are doing. Image description "[b]Find & Replace[/b]" is self-explanatory. You find certain words here, know where they are, and can choose to replace them with another word. "[b]Diff View[/b]" is an alternative way of seeing your changes compared to the Live Page. "[b]Submit[/b]" is where you submit your edit to the reviewers team to check. Here's a few things can happen: "I can't submit!": You probably haven't logged in to the site yet or you are barred from making edit for whatever reason. "Nothing is happening!": You should check your internet speed and see if it is fine or not. Long QA: You now have a word limit of 500, go on with your reasonings and such for your changes. Stats are designed to hold any pair of Keys and Values (Handsome? Yes, Rushdown? False, ...). But here are some of the must-have Stats to have: Archetype: Rushdown? Reversal? etc. Difficulty: Very Easy/Easy/Moderate/Hard Health: 100? 85? etc. There can be extra optional Stats. Here's the allowed extra optional Stats as of now: Base Only: Yes (Full character do not have this Stat) Overpowered Character: Yes (Same rule for non-OP characters) Availability: No Longer in the Game (Apply to those who know)

Difficulty refer to the skill floor of the character. More specifically, the amount of time/skill required to learn AND use that character effectively at a beginner level. Simply knowing the kit would not count as mastering the skill floor for example. [i]Very Easy[/i]: This character is really simple and intuitive to use, so long as you have the knowledge and experience with the basic fundamentals of the game (Side Dash M1, Combo-ing, etc.) [i]Easy[/i]: This character is simple to understand and to make sense of/get used to. Though you would need something other than your basic knowledge of the fundamentals to use this character effectively such as learning the things that character can do. [i]Moderate[/i]: This character requires some amount of time before you can start to use their kit effectively. But knowing most of the fundamentals can help you out during the learning phase or even carry you through using this character, as they are not that complex/hard to get used to. [i]Hard[/i]: This character is an unintuitive one to use for anyone trying them out, it can either be a complex kit or some forced gimmick check that raise the entry bar. You can mix the difficulty adjacent to each other as needed. For example, Easy-Moderate or Moderate-Hard

Briefly tells you about the weaknesses and strengths of a character, how they function, what potential they have, and do so in a way that is engaging to read. Non-repetitive language and a prose that's extremely easy to read. What [color=hsl(3, 93%, 63%)]NOT[/color] to write, overall just way to vague and talks too opinionated rather than factual. Don't mention what "tier" they are in and don't say basic things like "they are bad". Every character in this game has enough to talk about to go in depth about playstyle for a few paragraphs at least

Image description Each character will have their own Combos tab. It will consist of three main parts: Read First, Combo Groups, and Combo Lists.
How to work with the Combos Tab

[b]Read First[/b] is where you clarify about the details of the Combos tab such as how damage are calculated, what's the thing to looks out for when performing these combos, etc. You should use this part both as an introduction to that character combo game, and a caution sign to a few things before going in.

In here, you can create as many groups as needed with the naming of your choice. In each group, you can create a [b]Combo Card[/b]; it contains the combo name, combo short description, long description, damage value, and a showcase video. The basic idea here is that, these cards will have the combos that are the main highlights for the group they belong in such as "Beginner Combos". It is recommened to create 3 Combo Groups as your starting point: [b][i]Beginner Combos, BnB Combos, and Advanced Combos[/i][/b]. Anything more than that is up to your choice, your reasoning, and the staff team decision.

In here, you will be able to create multiple tables about combos. The table have a title (aka starter) to indicate what is the move used to start a combo (it can be more flexible than this if you want). Because it is a table, you are recommended to put all possible combo routes concerning each table titles. For more details on what to enter in each fields, read below.

Image description The main parts: [i]Name[/i]: The combo name [i]One Line[/i]: A short one-sentence description of the combo [i]Route[/i]: You enter the route here. [b][i]MAKE SURE THAT THE INPUTS ARE PER LINE[/i][/b] like this [code]M1 (next line) M1 (next line) Skill 1[/code] unlike the Combo Block [i]Damage[/i]: The total damage the combo would do to an opponent with zero damage reduction; as a general rule, combo damage would not count passive regeneration but you can clarify that as needed in the Write Up [i]Difficulty[/i]: The range is [color=hsl(127, 59%, 58%)]Very Easy[/color]/[color=hsl(100, 100%, 75%)]Easy[/color]/[color=#83eb13]Medium[/color]/[color=#deeb13]Slightly Hard[/color]/[color=#ffa700]Hard[/color]/[color=#e26000]Very Hard[/color]/[color=hsl(3, 93%, 63%)]Extremely Hard[/color]/[color=hsl(295, 89.76%, 50.2%)]Demon Time[/color] [i]Video[/i]: You paste your certified video URL here, it will only accept videos uploaded to the Media Library. [i]Author credit[/i]: Absolutely optional. Furthermore, crediting is good honor practice, but combos or techs are not intellectual properties, so don't go around throwing a tantrum if someone perform your combos (different from the content creation context) [i]Write Up[/i]: In here, you use the Block Editor to write detailss as needed.

[i]A frame[/i] refer to the unit of time equal to 1/60th of a second. It helps in examining the specific details of a move such as is this move punishable on Block? is this Move faster than a 14f M1? etc.

Jujutsu Shenanigans run at a fixed speed of 60 fps server-side, so things such as When Hitbox spawn or Starting up a move are tied to these discrete 1/60th of a second time frame. You can imagine it as a flipbook that flips through 60 pages per second; When you use a Skill, the game takes 1 frame to activate it [code]Frame 0: Use Skill > Frame 1: Skill Activate[/code], this process take exactly 1/60th of a second (not accounting for ping speed). There is virtually no way for you to speed this up, you can't force the game to activate your skill earlier that 1/60th of a second Hence, a frame is the smallest possible unit of time that we can use to dive deep into the technical and detailed parts of a move. It provides the highest precision and accuracy, while not being vague such as "fast" or "punishable" or "around 0.5s".

Metadata and Stats of a move

[b]Move Name[/b]: The name of the move. [b]Input[/b]: The input(s) needed to perform the move. More details below. [b]Skill Type[/b]: The type of move (Blockbreaker, Gapcloser, ...). More details below. [b]Damage Type[/b]: The type of damage the move deals: Melee, Bullet, Explosion, Swarm, Domain/Uncounterable. This is checked with Mahoraga's Adaptation or Skill Builder. [b]Variant[/b]: What variant of the move is it (Ground, Air, Normal, Standard, etc.). More details below. [b]Media Src[/b]: The media source that will display the move. [b]Media Alt Text[/b]: If the Media Src failed to load in the media for whatever reason, the alt text is there to back it up. [b]How to put in the right things in the Input field[/b] As a general rule, the input of a move is the last input on the keyboard needed to be [b]pressed[/b] to perform the move, [b]specifically[/b] before the move's Hitbox or its main function comes out. Everything else will be attached to the side in a parentheses as a note: [s]Space + M1[/s] [color=hsl(127, 59%, 58%)]M1 (While holding Space)[/color], [s]1 + 2[/s] [color=hsl(127, 59%, 58%)]2 (Before 1 hit)[/color], [s]Air + 2[/s] [color=hsl(127, 59%, 58%)]2 (In the Air)[/color], [s]S + 2[/s] [color=hsl(127, 59%, 58%)]2 (While holding S)[/color], etc. If a move require multiple inputs to perform before its hitbox comes out or its main function is executed, you should put in the field appropiate input sequence connected by the plus sign: [color=hsl(127, 59%, 58%)]3 + 3[/color] [s]3 (Timed after using 3 once)[/s], [color=hsl(127, 59%, 58%)]1 + 3 + 2 + R[/color] [s]R (Use last after sequecing 1 and then 2 and then 3)[/s], etc. [b]How to put the right things in the Skill Type field[/b] A Skill Type describe its main usecases and functions. Here's the list of Skill Type: Combo Starter: The move is mainly used to start a combo on usage or after an M1 Combo Extender: The move is used inbetween combo to extend the combo or M1s Combo Ender: The move is mainly used to end a combo, and it's usually the last move to be used Combo Tool: The move defining feature is being a Combo Starter, Extender, and Ender all at once Combo Breaker: The move is mainly used to disrupt/interrupt your opponent combo Reversal: The move is mainly used to turn around the flow of the match, aka reseting neutral, notably this skill type can't disrupt an opponent combo, disticnt from Combo Breaker. Counter: The move has a counter window and is activated by getting hit, different from Reversal Close Range Blockbreaker: A blockbreaking move that is effective at close range aka M1 range Long Range Blockbreaker: A blockbreaking move that is effective at long range aka Frontdash range Mid Range Blockbreaker: A blockbreaking move that is effective at mid range aka Sidedash range Mobility: A movement move that move the user around the battlefield Gapcloser: A movement option that force the user be close to the opponent Neutral Skip: A move that skip the M1 trading aspect of the game and immediately create pressure and attack the opponent, usually from mid to far range Punish Tool: A move that is mainly used to punish opponent actions such as punishing a side dash, or punishing an endlag, etc. Feint: A move that feints other moves Mixup Tool: A move that is mainly used to mix up the opponent during a combo, which means the combo is usually green Debuff: A move that is defined by its ability to put a status effect on the opponent Buff: A move that is defined by its ability to put a status effect on yourself Install: A move that once used, give you a buffed moveset compared to the weaker original one Neutral Poke: A move that is mainly used to attack at mid-far range as a poke. It usually doesn't convert, but there are exceptions Everything: This move do everything (many things) More... You can mix these skill types as needed as a move usually has more than 1 main use case; You should use the slash "/" sign to seperate such as Combo Starter/Feint or Mobility/Combo Tool/Reversal
